doc.title: Sam Kininger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 27, 2011

title: Playing with Dave Matthews Band
summary: Relationship began opening for DMB with Soulive; sitting in with LeRoi Moore and Jeff Coffin.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Great, yeah. It was amazing. And I was good friends. Well you know our relationship with them started with Soulive. We went on tour opening up for them, like we did this southern tour and then I became friends with LeRoi, the saxophone player who passed away, and so we kind of just had a relationship with them. Whenever they would come through I would sit in and also now that Jeff Coffin is in the band, who I’ve been friends with, so if they’re ever around like in Albany or like that, we go check them out. It’s usually the same tunes. Like, [sings] “Hey what’d you say” that tune.
So they always have me play that one.
Is their music, it seems like the horn part and the violin part were fairly arranged. I mean they had worked it out beforehand.

Yeah. And a lot of it’s pretty, I wouldn’t say simple, but it’s yeah, it’s definitely a good arrangement. That sound, which is strange too, the sound of the violin with the saxophone too kind of gives Dave Mathews that unique sound of his band.
Yeah. I bet you have to pay attention to stay in tune with the violin player.

Yeah. Well they all have those really nice in-ear monitors that are all set up so you don’t really have to — like you can hear Dave Mathews talk like from the other side of the stage. That’s how sensitive they are. And everyone’s pretty much in tune.
